title: model-variant-skus-and-upgrade-paths-2027-09-14
author: Maya Chen
summary: A structured plan for defining, pricing, and operating model-variant SKUs including customer upgrade paths, migration playbooks, billing implications, and telemetry required for measuring SKU adoption and fidelity impact.
body:
Overview:

This document defines Redwood's approach to packaging model variants as discrete SKUs (stock-keeping units), the upgrade and downgrade paths customers will follow, and the operational and contractual implications of SKU changes. It is intended for product managers, sales engineering, legal, finance, and platform engineers who implement billing, rollouts, and telemetry.

Goals:
- Provide a consistent mapping from model variant capabilities and fidelity profiles to customer-facing SKUs.
- Enable predictable upgrade/downgrade flows with minimal customer disruption.
- Minimize billing disputes by making cost transitions explicit in contracts and invoices.
- Instrument telemetry and SLOs so product and ops can measure fidelity and cost outcomes after migrations.

Audience:
- Product: PMs owning model catalog and pricing.
- Engineering: billing, runtime, and deployment teams.
- Sales & Solutions: pricing guidance and migration support.
- Finance & Legal: contract language and revenue recognition.
- Customer Success: onboarding and migration playbooks.

Context and Rationale:
As we expand the variant catalog (quantized variants, trimmed-context models, efficient-decoder variants, high-fidelity variants), customers need a clear way to buy, pin, and move between variants without losing SLAs or being surprised by bills. Historically we have offered ad-hoc variant pricing; this doc prescribes SKU-level packaging to improve predictability and automation.

Definitions:
- SKU: a customer-facing billing item that maps to one or more model variant binaries and an associated fidelity profile.
- Variant: a particular model artifact (weights, quantization, runtime flags) with documented performance and quality profile.
- Fidelity profile: runtime configuration (max tokens, sampling defaults, generation budget) tied to perceived quality.

Principles:
1) One SKU ↔ one fidelity envelope: Each SKU represents a bounded fidelity envelope (e.g., "Balanced-4k", "Economy-16k", "High-Fidelity-8k").
2) Backwards compatibility for pinned routes: Customers can pin routes to a specific SKU-version; our rollout tooling will enforce compatible fallbacks.
3) Transparent cost deltas: Price differences between SKUs must be explicit in the product page and in the upgrade API response.
4) Safe defaults: Default plan migrations for self-serve customers should prefer cost-smoothing paths (pro rata guarantees, temporary credits).

SKU Catalog (illustrative):
| SKU handle | Short description | Typical use cases | Relative cost factor | Default SLO |
|------------|------------------|-------------------|----------------------|-----------|
| economy-16k | Quantized 4-bit variant with aggressive kernel optimizations | embeddings, bulk document processing | 0.4x | 99.5% p95 latency bound |
| balanced-8k | Mixed precision variant optimized for chat workloads | customer-facing chatbots | 1x | 99.9% p95 latency bound |
| fidelity-8k | Higher-precision variant with conservative sampling defaults | long-form generation, high-quality summarization | 1.8x | 99.9% p95 latency bound |
| premium-32k | Extended context with higher memory footprint and tuned kernels | retrieval-augmented generation for long documents | 3.2x | 99.95% p95 latency bound |

SKU Assignment Rules:
- A SKU maps to a primary runtime configuration and a list of compatible fallback variants.
- Each SKU must document the following fields in the variant registry: model_name, quantization, expected tokens/sec, default sampling params, memory footprint, supported sequence lengths.
- Billingly, SKUs are tied to meter dimensions: tokens_generated, tokens_consumed (input), and compute_seconds.

Upgrade and Downgrade Paths:
We define three upgrade patterns: self-serve, assisted, and contract-bound.

1) Self-serve (Typical SMB and PLG motion)
- Step 1: Customer selects new SKU in Console or API.
- Step 2: System validates compatibility (route pinning, model availability) and returns an estimated monthly delta.
- Step 3: Change is applied at the next billing boundary by default; customer can choose immediate change with pro-rata charge.
- Step 4: Monitor fidelity and cost signals for the first 72 hours; automatic rollback triggers if fidelity regression exceeds threshold (see Telemetry & Guards).

2) Assisted migration (Mid-market customers)
- Sales/SE author an uplift plan in the migration template.
- Engineering creates a canary route (5% traffic) on the target SKU and runs a 48–72 hour performance/fidelity check with the customer's signature.
- If OK, staged ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over configurable windows.

3) Contract-bound (Enterprise Dedicated/Private)
- Changes require an amendment to the reserved capacity contract; pricing and capacity impact reviewed by finance.
- On-prem/private installs: upgrade is scheduled as part of a maintenance window; customer can opt for fall-forward patching or in-place upgrade.

Telemetry & Guards (required signals):
- Fidelity delta: per-route disagreement rate measured against a golden prompt set (baseline). Alert if > 4% increase in unacceptable outputs in first 72 hours.
- Latency delta: p95 latency change > 15% triggers canary hold.
- Cost delta: projected spend change > 25% triggers secondary confirmation.
- Error rate: 5xx increase > 0.5% absolute triggers immediate rollback.

Implementation Checklist (Engineering):
1) Billing & Catalog
- Create SKU entries in billing catalog with meter IDs, human-readable name, and price tiers.
- Ensure invoice line-item mapping preserves SKU handle and variant-version.
2) Runtime & Routing
- Extend routing layer to understand SKU handle and map to runtime config.
- Implement fallback compatibility table per SKU.
3) Console & API
- Add SKU selector UI with clear cost delta preview and upgrade button.
- Expose an API endpoint: POST /v1/accounts/:id/sku-change { new_sku, effective_at, immediate: bool } that returns a change_id and projected charges.
4) Telemetry & Alerts
- Wire up fidelity comparisons to Redwood Signal.
- Implement an automated rollback controller that can flip the route to fallback SKU for the specified customer.
5) Contracts & Billing
- Add standard amendment language and pro-rata logic for immediate upgrades.

Customer communication templates (examples):
- Email subject: "Action required: confirm upgrade to <SKU> for <route>"
- Body: brief summary of benefits, projected monthly delta, timing options, support contact, and link to migration plan.

Sample API response (successful change request):
{
  "change_id": "chg_01G7XAB2",
  "new_sku": "fidelity-8k",
  "effective_at": "2027-10-01T00:00:00Z",
  "projected_monthly_delta_usd": "+420.00"
}

Operational playbook: rollback decision matrix:
- Immediate rollback: 5xx spike > 0.5% absolute OR fidelity delta > 10% in first 24 hours.
- Pause rollout: latency p95 degradation > 25% OR customer reports degraded user experience.
- Continue: all telemetry within thresholds for 72 hours.

Billing edge cases:
- Legacy reserved contracts: maintain current pricing until contract amendment processed.
- Pro-rata disputes: automatically apply a temporary credit if customer requests rollback within 48 hours of immediate change.
- Marketplace resellers: publish mapping of SKU handles to marketplace product IDs.

Acceptance criteria (for product sign-off):
- Billing catalog exposes SKUs and test invoices render SKU line items.
- API supports change requests and returns deterministic projections.
- Console shows cost preview and migration options.
- Telemetry guards detect regressions and automated rollback can be exercised in staging.
- Sales/Merchant playbooks and customer-facing FAQ are published.

Metrics to track post-launch (KPI):
- SKU adoption rate by cohort (30/90 day).
- Median upgrade time (selection -> effective).
- Percent of upgrades requiring manual SE assistance.
- Incidence of rollback and primary causes.
- Net revenue delta attributable to variant SKUs.

Open questions / Risks:
- Pricing granularity: do we expose per-token pricing differences or only SKU-level multipliers? (Recommendation: SKU-level multipliers with advanced per-token overrides for enterprise).
- Accounting treatment for pro-rata credits across reserved capacity. Finance to provide guidance.
- Operator complexity: Increasing SKU count increases routing matrix complexity; require a maximum of 8 active SKUs per major model family.

Rollout timeline (proposal):
- Q4 2027: pilot with "economy-16k" and "balanced-8k" for self-serve customers.
- Q1 2028: introduce "fidelity-8k" as assisted migration for mid-market.
- Q2 2028: enterprise uplift and contract amendment workflows; marketplace mappings.

Appendix: Sample migration checklist for SEs (short):
1) Run compatibility checker for customer routes.
2) Create canary route and validate golden prompt set.
3) Confirm billing projection and obtain customer approval.
4) Schedule ramp windows and configure telemetry hooks.
5) Monitor first 72 hours; escalate if auto-rollback triggers.
